name: Idris Vega-Acheampong
role: Remote drone and vehicle operations specialist — rigger
location: Glassway — corporate-adjacent retail district, heavy surveillance, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Idris Vega-Acheampong is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 44, scars map her face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immu — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a rigger out of Glassway, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Everyone who's worked with Idris Vega-Acheampong agrees on two things: she is worth the fee, and she is terrible company at dinner.

core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
core_desires: Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running
A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
psychology.secret: Idris Vega-Acheampong witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Uses old pre-collapse slang that nobody else remembers
Pauses mid-sentence to listen — combat habit that bleeds into conversation
example_lines: "I have eyes in every district. Most of them are on wings."
"The drone doesn't care about your feelings. Neither do I."
"Remote operation means I'm everywhere and nowhere. It's very convenient."

story_hooks: A crew member from Idris Vega-Acheampong's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
A Tier 4 executive offers Idris Vega-Acheampong a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
The fixer who handles Idris Vega-Acheampong's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned
narrative_function: Idris Vega-Acheampong is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
augmentations: Internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immune to gas attacks. Internal drug synthesizer — produces combat stims and medical compounds on demand
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.

weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions
poor impulse control in specific triggers
risk-averse to the point of missed opportunities

decision_rules: Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Predatory focus. Threats are problems, and problems have solutions. The solution is usually kinetic.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Shutdown. Freezes for 2-3 seconds while the system resets, then acts with mechanical precision. Those frozen seconds are the vulnerability.

contradictions: Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
habits: Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Eats the same meal before every job — superstition masquerading as preference
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
breaking_points: Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
Their body rejecting their cyberware — chrome rot, immune rejection, the nightmare scenario
